svg.text: A data-side TLB miss, a same-page follower, and the fill — where the latency goes
Two loads to one page arrive on different lanes. The second joins the first's miss-station entry, one walk serves both, and each replays through its own lane in arrival order.
LSU lanes (VA)
L1 MMU + miss station
socket / cluster tlb arbs
VX_tlb_l2 (cluster TLB)
VX_ptw (walkers)
L2 cache / memory
load A — lane 0, page P (VPN v)
CAM probe: no entry; MSHR probe: no live entry → cat_park
alloc slot s ← {vpn v, acc RD, amo 0}; token {lane 0, fields A}
lane 0 ready=1: the LSU sees the request accepted and moves on
tlb_reads++, tlb_misses++ (park fire)
load B — lane 2, same page P
CAM probe: still no entry; MSHR probe: slot s live → mshr_match → cat_park
join slot s: token {lane 2, fields B} queued behind A (QDEPTH=2, so this fills the queue)
a third same-page lane would hold (alloc_ready=0) until a token drains
load C — lane 1, page Q (cached)
cat_hit: PPN splice + tlb_perm_ok → out_pipe → L1 dcache. Nothing waits on the walk. (hit-under-miss)
C's translated request leaves the MMU the next cycle
tlb_bus req {id = s, acc, amo, vpn v}
socket arb 2:1 prepends mmu index; cluster arb prepends socket index
each arb level is a registered slice (OUT_BUF=3): ~1 cycle per hop, both directions
req {id = {socket, mmu, s}, …}
lookup pipe: LATENCY cycles (VX_pipe_buffer, one request per cycle)
retire: megapage CAM miss ∧ set array miss (row = set(v), tag compare per way)
→ tail_miss: allocate L2 MSHR slot k (or join a live same-VPN entry) with token = id
issue to the walker: ptw_if.req {id = k, acc, amo, vpn v}
an L2 hit would instead answer here: rsp {id, level, ppn, flags} through the
response arbiter, and the sequence resumes at step 8
ptw_if req {id = k, vpn v}
walk cache probe: tag = v ≫ LEVEL_BITS
miss → start at root: ppn = satp.PPN, level = PT_LEVELS−1
lowest idle walker takes it (disp_vpn/acc/amo recorded)
PTE fetch, level 1 (root table)
line data → walker selects its PTE word
non-leaf, valid → ppn ← pte.ppn, level ← 0
walk-cache write {tag(v) → ppn} as the walk steps into its last level
PTE fetch, level 0
leaf, aligned → RESP {id = k, fault 0, level 0, ppn, flags}
walk-fill {id = k, level, ppn, flags}
install into the set array (level 0) or the megapage CAM (level ≥ 1); MRU bump
drain slot k: one response per attached token, through the response arbiter
rsp {id = {socket, mmu, s}, …}
tlb_bus rsp {id = s, level, ppn, flags} — arbs peel their index bits
install {level, v, ppn, flags} into the CAM; slot s drains: token A then token B, one per cycle
each replay re-splices its VA and re-checks its own permission, then takes its lane's out_pipe → L1 dcache (PA)
A and B leave translated, in arrival order; a faulted walk would kill them instead (zeroed load reply)
